Route: BRD4 + CRBN + short amide-ether linker + Western blot DC50/Dmax + minimum controls
DC50: >85% degradation at 100 nM in MV4-11 (18 h); DC50/5h ~500 nM in HiBiT-HEK293
When_to_Use: First pass; baseline; learning full workflow
Why_Not_Default: None - this is the starting point

Route: BRD4 + VHL + PEG3 + Western blot + cisMZ1 control
When_to_Use: After Tier 1 CRBN baseline works; teaches E3 choice effects; avoids CRBN neosubstrate off-targets
Why_Not_Default: Requires VHL expression; VHL-mutant RCC lines inactive; needs working Tier 1 comparator

DC50: DC50/5h ~10 nM for BRD4BD1; ~50 nM for BRD4BD2
When_to_Use: After Tier 1 shows degradation; teaches linker/permeability effects
Why_Not_Default: Requires working Tier 1 comparator; dBET6 paper is mechanistic (BET elongation) not PROTAC design-focused

Route: AR + CRBN + clinical precedent (different target same E3)
Readout: Western blot DC50/Dmax + PSA PD biomarker
When_to_Use: After Tier 1 BRD4 baseline works; branching to hormone receptor targets
Why_Not_Default: Complex warhead synthesis; restricted to AR+ cell lines; no simple commercially available PROTAC-ready binder

Route: Full concentration series + hook-effect modeling + ternary complex assay
When_to_Use: After initial degradation confirmed; teaches PROTAC-specific pharmacology
Why_Not_Default: Requires plate reader or NanoBRET instrumentation

Route: Novel E3 (DCAF1) + validated target binder + standard linker
When_to_Use: Only after Tier 1 and Tier 2 mastered; for overcoming CRBN resistance
Why_Not_Default: DCAF1 ligand affinity and tissue expression less validated; DC50 worse than CRBN-based BTK PROTACs

When_to_Use: Only with experienced team and established infrastructure
